authority_model.rule: CI verifies repository state and evidence; it is not described as preventing a network transfer that already occurred.

dedup.rationale: Per-stack scripts must delegate to harness/shared; see harness/shared/check_dedup.py

py_compat.rationale: Minimum runtime is derived from the CI python-version matrix; see harness/shared/check_py_compat.py

gates.rationale: Anti-vacuity population floors for harness/shared/check_dedup.py and harness/shared/check_py_compat.py (docs/specs/attested-execution-isolation.md R-AEI-3, AC-4), read through policy_loader.gate_floors. Both gates exited 0 against an empty tree and printed '[PASS] 0 per-stack script(s)' and '[PASS] 0 file(s) compatible' -- a report a reader cannot tell apart from a real pass, which is the same vacuity defect traceability.min_discovered_requirement_ids exists to catch. dedup_min_scripts is the number of per-stack scripts the gate must actually check (20: ten shims in each of harness/node/scripts and harness/jvm/scripts); py_compat_min_files is the number of first-party Python files it must actually scan (298, the committed tree when this floor was measured). Each is a ratchet: raise it as the population grows, never lower it so a shrinking population passes. Deleting a governed script or module is therefore a deliberate, reviewed edit to this block rather than a silent reduction in what the gates cover. This is a new top-level block rather than a key inside dedup/py_compat because DEC-043 makes an absent key inside an adopted block a PolicyError for every adopter policy that predates it (the R-AEI-11 reason); the built-in default for an adopter with no policy file at all is 0, which leaves both gates behaving exactly as they do today.

synthesis.rationale: Synthesis policy gates (INV-9..INV-15). max_repair_cycles is the budget for the repair loop (INV-12). lats_enabled must be false until ablation gate in tasks.md §Evaluation Gate is passed (INV-15). critique_schema_version pins the versioned critique schema (INV-11). python_write_suffixes names the target suffixes that make a generated write Python, and so which writes are checked against prohibited_imports at all; `language` and `validate_syntax` are model-supplied tool arguments and may not decide it. `.pyi` is deliberately excluded: a stub is never executed and legitimately names modules it only mentions in signatures. Added under DEC-065 after a review found .pyw bypassed the check (PR #120).

traceability.rationale: Scope and ratchet for harness/shared/governance/check_traceability.py (DEC-065, docs/specs/graph-engineering-adoption.md R-GEA-1/R-GEA-1b). The gate resolved its config and globs against the process CWD and ran from harness/node, so it read 6 requirement IDs while docs/specs held 412 sharing none of them, and printed 'traceability: passed'. min_discovered_requirement_ids is the anti-vacuity floor a repository-scoped run must clear, so 'the gate is pointed at the wrong corpus' fails instead of passing; it applies only where a traceability config declares scope 'repository', leaving per-stack configs unchanged. max_uncited_contract_requirement_ids is a ratchet over contract-spec IDs missing an implementation or test citation: it may be lowered as citations land and never raised, so the backlog is visible and cannot grow. Its value is 222, measured after NS-39 citations; the high-water mark may only fall, and the composition is stated because the number is the whole control: 222 is the corpus as it stood before this change, and the +1 is R-GEA-5 -- graph-engineering-adoption's own requirement that a tokens-per-turn baseline be recorded before any code-property graph is built. That requirement is deliberately unimplemented, so it has nothing to cite, and pretending otherwise by citing it somewhere convenient is the failure this gate exists to catch. Every other requirement that spec declares is cited on both sides. SPEC_TEMPLATE.md is excluded from the corpus, matching validate_specs.py and validate_plan.py, so all three gates read one corpus. program_plan_class names the class a document declares via spec_class_marker when its requirement IDs are scheduled work with nothing yet to cite; default_spec_class is the strict branch a document with no declaration falls into.

denial_rate.rationale: Ceiling and population floor for harness/shared/governance/denial_rate.py (DEC-067, docs/specs/attested-execution-isolation.md R-AEI-2). The ceiling is a ratchet: it may be lowered as denials are closed, never raised. It stands at 0.0 because DEC-067 closed every false denial the corpus held -- 13 of 36 before it, including the python -m ruff and python -m mypy forms CLAUDE.md mandates under DEC-013. The floor stops the rate being driven down by deleting corpus entries; the corpus is a protected path for the same reason. A new top-level block rather than a key inside an adopted one, because DEC-043 makes an absent key in an adopted block a PolicyError for every adopter policy that predates it.

evidence.rationale: Bound on in-memory / JSONL evidence entries produced by a governed ExecutionBroker (docs/specs/attested-execution-isolation.md R-AEI-4, R-AEI-6, AC-8, C-AEI-2). A new top-level block rather than a key inside an adopted one, because DEC-043 makes an absent key in an adopted block a PolicyError for every adopter policy that predates it. The sink must lie outside the agent workspace and outside protected_paths (R-AEI-5).

execution.rationale: Two-state selector for governed execution (docs/specs/attested-execution-isolation.md R-AEI-11, AC-11). brokered runs commands through ExecutionBroker; refuse returns BLOCKED before spawn. A new top-level block rather than a key inside an adopted one, because DEC-043 makes an absent key in an adopted block a PolicyError for every adopter policy that predates it. Absent block (adopter policies that predate it) defaults to brokered.
